children: Thirty-year Japanese government bonds look worth buying with yields above 4%, RBC BlueBay Asset Management fixed-income CIO Mark Dowding says in a note. "We continue to highlight attractive structural value in 30-year JGBs above 4%," he says. He adds that there is "a sense that Japanese policymakers are taking the selloff in JGBs seriously, now that 10-year yields have breached 3%." Dowding also points to speculation that the Government Pension Investment Fund will substantially revise upwards its holdings of Japanese bonds within its asset allocation. The 30-year JGB yield hit a peak of 4.207% on Wednesday and last trades at 3.967%, according to LSEG. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
